newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand seeks mechanism to counter baht attacks.
newsitem.headline: Thailand seeks mechanism to counter baht attacks.

text.p: Thai Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan said on Friday the government would find an effective mechanism to ward off future market attacks against the baht.

Amnuay told reporters: "We need more established measures to deal with any future attacks on the baht. Something like what they have in Singapore which stops its people from speculating in its own currency."
"We have a free and open market but we do not open our market in order to let people bully us," the minister said.

The baht faced heavy speculative attacks early this week forcing Thai and Singapore central banks to jointly intervene on behalf of the Thai currency. Some other regional central banks also intervened, dealers said.
Amnuay said a weaker baht may benefit the country's trade and investment but the currency should not be pushed down by speculators.

He said the Thai authorities have been successful in restoring baht stability partly through its squeeze on short-term funds which raised the cost for foreign speculators to bet against the baht to an equivalent of nearly 1,000 percent per year.

Amnuay said the government would move to boost the battered Thai stock market next week, including a plan for the Securities Finance Corp (SFC) to buy equities margin loan accounts from cash-strapped brokerage firms for three years.
He said SFC would soon float five billion baht ($192 million) of debentures to raise funds for refinancing the margin loans.
Fifty percent of the paper would be absorbed by members of the Stock Exchange of Thailand and the rest by financial institutions, he said.
